questions.prompt: What money is used in Sweden?

hints.nudge: Money names often come from a country’s own words. The other three are spent in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Sweden article.

questions.proof: The currency remains the Swedish krona (Swedish crown).

questions.prompt: Which country has the capital city Stockholm?

hints.nudge: Every country has one capital city. Find the city in the question on a map, then see which country it sits in.
hints.whereToLook: Look on the Atlas: find the city, then see which country it sits in.

questions.proof: The capital city of Sweden is Stockholm.

hints.nudge: A continent is one of the great land masses of the world. Find Sweden on the Atlas and see which land mass it sits on.
hints.whereToLook: Find Sweden on the Atlas and see which land mass it sits on.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries covers the most ground?

hints.nudge: Area is how much ground a country covers, not how many people live there. A small crowded country can still be small.
hints.whereToLook: Compare the four on the Atlas. Area means how much ground a country covers.

questions.proof: By area: Sweden about 447,425 square kilometres; Nepal about 147,181 square kilometres; Slovakia about 49,034 square kilometres; Estonia about 45,335 square kilometres.

questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Sweden?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Sweden article.

questions.proof: Sweden's capital city is Stockholm, which is also Sweden's largest city, with almost one million people.
